existing.description: The King-Morgridge Scholars Program is a four-year, full-tuition scholarship at the University of Wisconsin-Madison for international students from Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, South Asia and Southeast Asia who are committed to applying their talents toward poverty alleviation around the globe. Scholars receive a full-time, four-year/eight-semester award covering tuition and fees, on-campus room and board, health insurance, airfare and a stipend for miscellaneous expenses, with six scholarships awarded each year. Applicants must apply to UW-Madison International Admissions by November 1, 2026 and submit the Wisconsin Scholarship Hub KMSP application by November 15, 2026 for Cohort 11 (Fall 2027 entry). Scholars must maintain a 3.0 GPA, take at least 12 credits a semester, and participate actively in the program.
eligibility: Citizen of or from Africa, Caribbean, Latin America, South Asia, or Southeast Asia.
Committed to applying talents toward poverty alleviation in home country.
Must apply for admission to UW-Madison by November 1.
Must submit separate King-Morgridge scholarship application by November 15.
existing.eligibility_summary: Students from Africa, Caribbean, Latin America, South Asia, or Southeast Asia; demonstrated academic success and commitment to poverty alleviation in home country; enterprising, creative, dedicated.
requirements: Maintain a minimum 3.0 grade point average
Complete at least 12 credits as a full-time student each semester

Actively participate in program activities including individual advising appointments, program meetings and other scheduled programming, respond to KMSP communications promptly and submit absence requests in advance
Participate in Orientation and the Wisconsin Experience Seminar during the first fall semester
Follow all University policies and state and federal laws
documents: Essays demonstrating commitment to poverty alleviation
existing.english_requirement: As per UW-Madison undergraduate admission requirements.
application_method: Apply to UW-Madison by November 1, then submit separate KMSP application via Wisconsin Scholarship Hub (WiSH) by November 15
existing.selection_notes: Six scholarships are made each year. Selection is made by the UW-Madison Office of Admissions and Recruitment together with KMSP staff, who actively recruit candidates from Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America and South and Southeast Asia, review applications for admission to UW-Madison, and participate in the selection of candidates for the program. Selected scholars are chosen for their drive, academic success and commitment to addressing problems of poverty in their own countries.
existing.best_fit: Exceptional students from Africa, Caribbean, Latin America, South Asia, and Southeast Asia committed to poverty alleviation.
existing.notes: Six scholarships awarded per year. Must be admitted to UW-Madison first. Selection based on drive, academic success, and commitment to addressing poverty. Cohort-based program with leadership development.
existing.application_period: Fall entry; admission due November 1, scholarship due November 15
existing.program_type: Donor-endowed university scholarship for international undergraduates
